sections.body: Digital Cinema (D-Cinema) is a standardized ecosystem for packaging, securing, distributing, and exhibiting motion-imaging content in theatrical environments. It defines interoperable building blocks such as composition metadata, MXF track files for picture and sound, subtitles/captions, packaging and asset identifiers, and a security model for protected content and keys. In practice, D-Cinema workflows connect mastering and distribution deliverables (e.g., DCDM and DCP) with operational requirements in cinemas, enabling consistent playback behavior across equipment vendors and venues.

sections.body: IMF is a file-based media format that simplifies the delivery and storage of audio-visual masters intended for multiple territories and platforms. It is particularly well-adapted for delivery to today’s global content platforms. IMF works with any finished audio-visual masters, including long-form movies, episodic content, advertisements, short-form content, etc. It is extensible, uses proven technologies and benefits from many open source and commercial implementations.

sections.body: Captions, subtitles, and accessibility technologies enable the representation of spoken dialogue, non-speech information, and alternative language or sensory experiences for audiences with diverse needs. Across theatrical, broadcast, and online workflows, these systems encompass timed text formats, rendering and styling models, signaling mechanisms, and interchange practices designed to support comprehension, localization, and accessibility compliance. In practice, accessibility solutions span authoring, packaging, distribution, and playback, integrating with media formats and delivery ecosystems to ensure consistent, interoperable presentation across platforms and devices.
